[NextItNet (WSDM 2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) establishes stacked residual dilated causal convolutions for short- and long-range dependencies. [SkipRec (AAAI 2021)](https://cdn.aaai.org/ojs/16518/16518-13-20012-1-2-20210518.pdf) adds user-adaptive block retention/skipping, learned through Gumbel-softmax or reinforcement learning. Its softmax selects skip/retain actions; it does not perform positionwise softmax aggregation of intermediate states. These sources establish related precedents, but do not establish an exact precedent for the proposed gate. Receptive-field reasoning: at stride one, maximum span is R=1+Σ_j(k_j−1)d_j over actual convolution layers. Intermediate residual states have overlapping, nested dependencies, rather than independent temporal bands; repeated dilations do not reset accumulated context.

A reproducible proposed extension: collect block outputs h[t,l], set z[t,l]=LayerNorm_D(h[t,l]), logits a[t,l]=w_lᵀz[t,l]+b_l, α[t,:]=softmax_l(a[t,:]), and output f[t]=Σ_l α[t,l]z[t,l]. Initialize w_l=0 and b_l=0 for uniform depth weights; explicitly report any deepest-layer bias instead. Feature normalization controls scale differences between depths. This is one jointly trained NextItNet network; all blocks still execute, unlike computational skipping.

Preserve causality with left-only convolution padding and gates computed exclusively from same-position causal states. Zero padding embeddings and reapply the nonpadding mask after each convolution/normalization/residual stage and aggregation; exclude padded targets from loss. Read the final nonpadding index, never count−1 for left-padded histories. Use [LayerNorm(D)](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.LayerNorm.html) on B×L×D tensors, normalizing channels only. Avoid normalization across time: [BatchNorm1d](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.batchnorm.BatchNorm1d.html) pools training statistics across sequence positions, creating future-position leakage; temporal InstanceNorm/GroupNorm and LayerNorm over (L,D) have the same concern.
